x.t: Helpers at work after Cyclone Akvan reaches Odisha
b: Because of [[cyclone|Cyclone]] Akvan, helpers in Odisha moved about 3.7 lakh people to safety. A lakh is one hundred thousand.
The storm came onto land near [[gopalpur|Gopalpur]] on Friday 20 November. The storm has become weaker. Officials said no big damage had been reported so far.
More heavy rain was expected in Odisha. More than 400 teams were ready to help. Some teams were sent to clear away rainwater.

o.t: Helpers at work as Cyclone Akvan weakens over Odisha
b: About 3.7 lakh (370,000) people in Odisha were moved to safety because of [[cyclone|Cyclone]] Akvan, officials said. Thousands of cyclone [[shelter|shelters]] had been set up. More than 400 teams were in place to help, including rescue teams, fire service teams and tree-cutting teams.

Akvan crossed the coast near [[gopalpur|Gopalpur]], in Ganjam district, on the morning of Friday 20 November. It has weakened from a severe cyclonic storm to a cyclonic storm, a less powerful kind of storm. Weather experts expected it to keep weakening into a deep depression, an even weaker stage.
Officials said no major damage had been reported so far. More heavy rain was expected across Odisha. Teams were sent to clear away rainwater where it had collected, and tree-cutting teams were ready.

stories.think: Many people moved to safe places because of the storm. How does your family get ready when a big storm or heavy rain is coming?

quiz.q: Near which place did Cyclone Akvan cross the coast?

x.t: A cheetah from Botswana has four cubs in India
b: A mother cheetah has had four [[cubs|cubs]]. They were born on Friday 20 November at [[kuno|Kuno National Park]] in India.
The cubs were born [[in-the-wild|in the wild]]. Their mother had lived in the wild for more than four months.
She was brought to India from [[botswana|Botswana]]. With the new cubs, India now has 62 cheetahs.

o.t: Cheetah from Botswana has four cubs in the wild at Kuno
b: A female cheetah known by the code name KOMG 3 gave birth to four [[cubs|cubs]] [[in-the-wild|in the wild]] on Friday 20 November. The cubs were born at [[kuno|Kuno National Park]] in Madhya Pradesh. KOMG 3 had spent more than four months in the wild before her cubs arrived, so she was living freely in nature.
KOMG 3 is about two and a half years old. She was brought to India from [[botswana|Botswana]]. She is the first female cheetah from Botswana to give birth in India.
The news was shared on the social media site X by [[bhupender-yadav|Bhupender Yadav]], India's environment minister. With the four new cubs, the number of cheetahs in India has gone up to 62.

stories.think: If you could watch the four cheetah cubs grow up, what would you most like to find out about them?

quiz.q: Which country was the mother cheetah brought from?

x.t: New world records for parking, painting and skipping
b: People in many places set new [[world-record|world records]] for Guinness World Records Day. A stunt driver parked a car balanced on two wheels.
A painter made a painting of the Statue of Liberty in 43.5 seconds. In Dubai, 12 cars did a trick called [[donut|donuts]] in one circle.
Other people set records for skipping with a rope. One person did 249 skips in one minute, wearing flip-flops!

o.t: Two-wheel parking and speed painting among new world records
b: People around the world set new [[world-record|world records]] for Guinness World Records Day 2026. Stunt driver Alastair Moffatt set a record for parking a car in the tightest space while driving it balanced on two wheels.

Performance painter David Garibaldi set a record by painting a picture of the Statue of Liberty in 43.5 seconds. In Dubai, the 777 Drifting Team had 12 cars doing [[donut|donuts]] at the same time in a single circle.
In Japan, Kirato Hitaka set three [[rope-skipping|rope-skipping]] records, and a person in Indonesia did 249 rope skips in one minute while wearing flip-flops.

stories.think: If you could try to set a safe record, like skipping or stacking, what would you choose, and how would you practise?

x.t: India bat well after New Zealand score 368 runs
b: India are playing New Zealand in a [[test-match|Test match]] in Wellington. On Friday 20 November, New Zealand finished batting with 368 runs. Henry Nicholls made 175 runs.
Then India batted. Yashasvi Jaiswal scored 85 runs from 89 balls. KL Rahul was still batting on 52 runs.
By the end of the day, India had 159 runs. Only one Indian batter was out. India were 209 runs behind New Zealand's score.

o.t: Jaiswal and Rahul lead India's reply after New Zealand make 368
b: New Zealand's batting ended on 368 runs on day two of the opening [[test-match|Test match]] of the series against India, on Friday 20 November. The match is being played at the [[basin-reserve|Basin Reserve]] in Wellington. Henry Nicholls finished on 175 [[not-out|not out]], which means nobody got him out, and Glenn Phillips scored 118.

India then batted. Their openers, the first two batters, were Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul. They added 130 runs together before Jaiswal was out. Jaiswal scored 85 off 89 balls. When play stopped for the day, Rahul was 52 not out and Devdutt Padikkal was 16 not out.
India ended the day on 159 for 1, which means 159 runs with one batter out, or one [[wicket|wicket]] lost. They were 209 runs behind New Zealand's score of 368.

stories.think: Jaiswal and Rahul added 130 runs together. Why do you think working well with a partner helps in sport?

quiz.q: How many runs behind New Zealand were India at the end of day two?

x.t: Indian share prices rise, with banks leading the way
b: The [[sensex|Sensex]] and the [[nifty|Nifty 50]] went up on Friday 20 November. They are numbers that show how shares in big Indian companies are doing. A share is a small part of a company that people can buy.
Shares in banks led the rise. This month so far, people from other countries bought more Indian shares than ever before.

o.t: Sensex and Nifty rise as foreign investors buy a record amount
b: The [[sensex|Sensex]] is a [[stock-index|stock market index]] that tracks 30 large companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), a place where shares in companies are bought and sold. A share is a small part of a company. An index like this shows how the prices of a group of shares are doing. On Friday 20 November the Sensex ended the day at 83,919.71. That was a rise of 1.08%.
The [[nifty|Nifty 50]], which tracks 50 top companies on another stock exchange, the National Stock Exchange (NSE), ended the day at 25,800.60. That was a rise of 1.12%. Bank shares led the rise.
Foreign investors, meaning buyers of shares from other countries, have bought a record amount of Indian shares so far in November. That means more than in any month before.

x.t: Wet track stops lap times at Las Vegas race practice
b: [[formula-1|Formula 1]] drivers practised for the [[grand-prix|Las Vegas Grand Prix]]. The track was very wet in the first practice. No driver set a [[lap|lap]] time.
A lap time shows how long a car takes to go once round the track.
In the second practice, George Russell was the fastest. Pierre Gasly was second. Charles Leclerc was third.

o.t: Russell fastest in Las Vegas practice after wet first session
b: [[formula-1|Formula 1]] drivers took to the track for practice at the [[grand-prix|Las Vegas Grand Prix]], one of the races of the 2026 season. A practice session is a time before the race when teams get their cars ready. In the first practice session the conditions were so wet that not a single driver set a [[lap|lap]] time, which is the time a car takes to go once round the track.
In the second practice session, George Russell of the Mercedes team was the fastest. His best lap was 1:47.272, which means 1 minute and 47.272 seconds.
Pierre Gasly of the Alpine team was second, only 0.071 seconds slower than Russell. Charles Leclerc of the Ferrari team was third, about a third of a second slower than Russell.

stories.think: Wet weather changed what the drivers could do. Has the weather ever changed your plans, and what did you do instead?

cyclone: A powerful storm with strong winds that spin around, and heavy rain.
A powerful storm in which strong winds move in a circle, often bringing heavy rain. Weather experts describe cyclones by strength: a severe cyclonic storm is stronger than a cyclonic storm.
gopalpur: A place on the coast of Odisha.
A place on the coast of Odisha, in Ganjam district.
shelter: A safe place that protects people from bad weather or danger.
A place or building that protects people from bad weather or danger. A cyclone shelter is a building where people can stay safe during a cyclone.
cubs: Young animals, such as young cheetahs, lions or bears.
The young of some meat-eating animals, such as cheetahs, lions and bears.
kuno: A national park in Madhya Pradesh, a state of India.
A national park in the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh. KOMG 3, a cheetah brought from Botswana, lives there.
in-the-wild: Living free in nature, not controlled by people.
Living in a natural place that is not controlled by people.
botswana: The country the mother cheetah was brought from.
A country. KOMG 3, the mother of the new cubs, was brought to India from there.
bhupender-yadav: India's Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
world-record: The best, biggest or fastest that anyone in the world has done.
The best result ever officially recorded anywhere in the world for a particular feat.
donut: A car trick where the car spins round.
A driving trick in which a car spins round.
rope-skipping: Jumping over a rope as it swings under your feet.
Jumping over a rope each time it is swung over your head and under your feet.
test-match: A cricket match between the teams of two countries. It can last up to five days.
A cricket match played between the teams of two different countries, typically lasting five days.
basin-reserve: A cricket ground in Wellington, New Zealand.
A cricket ground in Wellington, New Zealand, where New Zealand and India are playing the opening match of their Test series.
not-out: In cricket, a batter who is not out was never got out.
In cricket, a batter who is not out has not been dismissed. This happens when the team's innings ends, or play stops for the day, while they are still batting.
wicket: In cricket, a team takes a wicket when it gets a batter out.
In cricket, taking a wicket means getting a batter out. A score of 159 for 1 means 159 runs with one batter out.
draw: A way of choosing by chance who will play whom.
A way of deciding by chance which teams will play each other in a competition.
nyon: The town where the draw was held.
The town where the draw for the quarter-finals was held.
nations-league: A football contest for the national teams of Europe.
The UEFA Nations League, a competition for the national teams of Europe.
semi-final: One of the last two matches before the final.
One of the two matches that decide who plays in the final.
sensex: A number that tracks 30 large companies in India.
A stock market index that tracks 30 large companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
nifty: A number that tracks 50 top companies in India.
A stock market index that tracks the top 50 companies on the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
stock-index: A number that shows how the prices of shares in a group of companies are doing.
A measure that tracks how the shares of a chosen group of companies are doing, such as the 30 companies in the Sensex or the 50 in the Nifty 50.
formula-1: The top contest in car racing.
The most important world championship in motor racing.
grand-prix: A big car race. The name is French for 'great prize'.
One of a series of important international motor races. The name is French for 'great prize'.
lap: One time all the way round a track.
One complete trip round a racetrack.
jpl: A NASA centre in California. The Voyager 1 mission is run from there.
A NASA laboratory in California. The Voyager mission is run from there.
deep-space-network: NASA's big antennas that keep track of faraway spacecraft.
NASA's network of giant radio antennas, with sites in California, near Madrid in Spain and near Canberra in Australia. It keeps track of Voyager 1.
coffin: A box in which a dead person is buried.
A box in which a dead person is buried.
export: Something a country sells to another country.
Something a country sells to other countries. To export means to sell goods or services to another country.
light-day: How far light travels in one whole day. It is a very long way.
A unit of distance: how far light travels in 24 hours, about 25.9 billion kilometres.
interstellar: The space between the stars. Voyager 1 became the first spacecraft to enter it, in 2012.

in-akvan.ctx: Akvan, which had been a severe cyclonic storm, weakened to a cyclonic storm around the time it crossed the Odisha coast near Gopalpur, in Ganjam district. About 3.7 lakh people were moved to safety, thousands of shelters were ready, and more than 400 teams, including rescue, fire service and tree-cutting teams, were in place. Weather experts expected Akvan to keep weakening into a deep depression, while more heavy rain was expected across Odisha.
in-akvan.ask: Heavy rain was still expected after Akvan weakened. Some people think families should stay in shelters until officials say it is fully safe, even if that takes days. Others think people should be able to go home as soon as the strong winds have passed, so they can look after their homes and get back to normal life. Who should decide when it is time to go home, and how?

in-cheetah-cubs.ctx: KOMG 3 is the first female cheetah from Botswana to give birth in India. She had spent more than four months in the wild at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh before the cubs were born. This is the second recorded birth in the wild since the programme to bring cheetahs to India began in 2022, and 43 of India's 62 cheetahs were born in India.
in-cheetah-cubs.ask: Some people think animals brought to a new country should be released into the wild as soon as they can, so they live freely and raise young on their own. Others think they should stay longer in places where people can look after them closely. Which do you think is better for the animals, and why?

g-records-day.ctx: Records were set in several places for this year's Guinness World Records Day, including Dubai, Japan and Indonesia. They ranged from car stunts to speed painting and rope skipping.

Some people think record books should include risky stunts, because skilled performers show what is possible. Others think record books should focus on records that are safer to copy, because young fans may try them. Should record books include risky stunts?

bigStory.t: How far is one light-day from home?
bigStory.sub: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, reached one light-day from Earth on Wednesday

x.why: A spacecraft that left Earth in 1977 is still travelling. This week it got so far away that light needs a whole day to reach it.

o.why: A spacecraft launched in 1977 is still travelling, and its team on Earth still talks to it. This week it reached a distance so great that a radio signal, moving at the speed of light, needs 24 hours to get there.

facts: about one light-day: how far light travels in 24 hours
how long a radio signal from Earth now takes to reach it
the day it reached one light-day

days.o: NASA launched Voyager 1 on 5 September 1977. It flew past Jupiter in 1979 and Saturn in 1980, and in 1990 it took a picture of Earth known as the Pale Blue Dot. In 2012 it entered interstellar space, the space between the stars. It is run from NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California.
days.x: Voyager 1 is a spacecraft. It left Earth in 1977. It flew past the planets Jupiter and Saturn. In 1990 it took a picture of Earth from very far away.

days.o: A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, about 25.9 billion kilometres. Light reaches the Moon in about 1.3 seconds, and sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth. After sunset today, Tuesday 17 November, NASA invites people to flash VGR, Voyager's three-letter call sign, in Morse code towards the sky with a torch.
days.x: A light-day is how far light travels in one day. Sunlight reaches us in about 8 minutes. After sunset today, people can flash a torch for Voyager. Ask a grown-up to help.

days.o: NASA worked out that Voyager 1 would reach one light-day from Earth on Wednesday 18 November. No spacecraft has travelled this far before. A radio signal now takes about 24 hours to reach it, and its reply takes another day to come back. Voyager 2 is expected to reach one light-day in 2035.
days.x: On Wednesday, Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth. No spacecraft has gone this far before. A message now takes about a day to get there.

days.o: NASA talks to Voyager 1 by radio through its Deep Space Network, a set of giant radio antennas at three sites: Goldstone in California, near Madrid in Spain and near Canberra in Australia. The sites are placed around the world so that they can keep in contact with a spacecraft as Earth turns. Each site has one antenna that is 70 metres across. A radio signal now takes about 24 hours to reach Voyager 1, and its reply takes another 24 hours to come back, so a message and its answer make a two-day round trip.
days.x: NASA talks to Voyager 1 with radio signals. It uses giant radio antennas in California, Spain and Australia. A message takes about a day to reach Voyager 1. The reply takes another day to come back.

days.o: On Wednesday 18 November Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth. Its power source makes about 4 watts less every year, so NASA has been switching off instruments to save power. Even after it falls silent, it will keep travelling. It will take about 300 years to reach the inner edge of a distant region called the Oort Cloud. In about 40,000 years it is expected to pass another star. It carries a Golden Record with sounds, music and images from Earth, and greetings in 55 languages.
days.x: On Wednesday, Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth. Its power gets a little weaker every year. Even when it falls silent, it will keep travelling. It carries a Golden Record with sounds, music and pictures from Earth.

x.t: Mercury, the planet closest to the Sun

A year on Mercury is short. It lasts only 88 Earth days. Mercury has no moons.
Days on Mercury are very hot. Nights on Mercury are very cold.
x.remember: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun. It is also the smallest planet.

o.t: Mercury, the planet closest to the Sun
b: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun. It is also the smallest planet in our solar system. It travels around the Sun once every 88 Earth days, so a year on Mercury lasts only 88 Earth days. Mercury has no moons.

Being the closest planet to the Sun does not make Mercury the hottest planet. Its days are very hot: temperatures can rise to more than 400 degrees Celsius. Its nights are very cold: temperatures can fall to about minus 170 degrees Celsius or colder.

Only two spacecraft had visited Mercury before BepiColombo. They were called Mariner 10 and MESSENGER. BepiColombo, a mission of Europe and Japan, is due to enter orbit around Mercury, which means to begin circling it, on Saturday 21 November.
o.remember: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun and the smallest planet in our solar system. One year there lasts 88 Earth days.
o.q: How long is one year on Mercury?

hiddenWords.o: Coffin comes from kophinos, the Greek word for a basket. The word passed through Latin, as cophinus, and through French before it reached English.
Export comes from the Latin word exportare, which is made from ex and portare. Portare is the Latin word for to carry.
Grand prix is French for 'great prize'. The name comes from the Grand Prix de Paris, a horse race in Paris that began in 1863.
